## ARCHITECTURE (PowerPC Book I v2.01, local copy `_scratchpad/ppc_uisa_book1_v201.txt`)

* rlwimi: `r <- ROTL32((RS)32:63, SH); m <- MASK(MB+32, ME+32); RA <- (r & m) | ((RA) & ~m)`.
  ROTL32 rotates the low word and DUPLICATES it into both halves.  MASK(x, y) is 1s from x through
  y, **wrapping if x > y** (:578).  So when MB > ME the mask covers the whole high word and RA's high
  word becomes the rotated word; when MB <= ME the high word is untouched.
* rldimi: `r <- ROTL64((RS), sh); m <- MASK(mb, 63-sh); RA <- (r & m) | ((RA) & ~m)` — the mask
  wraps when mb > 63-sh.

## THE FIXES (uncommitted), `src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c`, both functions WHOLE, post-fix

```c
X(rldimi)
{
	uint32_t iw = ic->arg[0];
	int rs = (iw >> 21) & 31, ra = (iw >> 16) & 31;
	int sh = ((iw >> 11) & 31) | ((iw & 2) << 4);
	int mb = ((iw >> 6) & 31) | (iw & 0x20);
	int rc = ic->arg[0] & 1;
	int m, n = sh;                                   /* FIX: was `int m;` */
	uint64_t tmp, s = cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[rs];
	while (n-- != 0) {                               /* FIX: was `sh--`, which left sh = -1 */
		int b = (s >> 63) & 1;
		s = (s << 1) | b;
	}
	m = mb; tmp = 0;
	do {
		tmp |= ((uint64_t)1 << (63-m));
		m = (m + 1) & 63;                        /* FIX: was `m ++;` */
	} while (m != ((64 - sh) & 63));                 /* FIX: was `m != 63 - sh` */
	cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[ra] &= ~tmp;
	cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[ra] |= (tmp & s);
	if (rc)
		update_cr0(cpu, cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[ra]);
}

X(rlwimi)
{
	uint32_t tmp = (uint32_t)reg(ic->arg[0]);        /* FIX: was MODE_uint_t tmp = reg(...) */
	MODE_uint_t ra = reg(ic->arg[1]);
	uint32_t iword = ic->arg[2];
	int sh = (iword >> 11) & 31;
	int mb = (iword >> 6) & 31;
	int me = (iword >> 1) & 31;
	int rc = iword & 1;

	tmp = sh ? ((tmp << sh) | (tmp >> (32-sh))) : tmp;

	/* (a 19-line comment: the wrapping mask selects the duplicated high word; a 32-bit
	   MODE_uint_t build keeps only the low word by unsigned-conversion semantics) */
	if (mb > me)                                     /* FIX: added, BEFORE the loop */
		ra = (ra & 0xffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)tmp << 32);

	for (;;) {
		uint64_t mask;
		mask = (uint64_t)1 << (31-mb);
		ra &= ~mask;
		ra |= (tmp & mask);
		if (mb == me)
			break;
		mb ++;
		if (mb == 32)
			mb = 0;
	}
	reg(ic->arg[1]) = ra;
	if (rc)
		update_cr0(cpu, ra);
}
```

**The defects fixed.**  rlwimi: a 64-bit `tmp` rotated as if 32-bit contaminated the low word with
high-word bits (`(tmp << sh) | (tmp >> (32-sh))` on 64 bits), and a wrapping mask never wrote the
high word.  rldimi: the rotate loop consumed `sh` (leaving -1), so the mask end was computed from
-1; and the mask loop did not wrap past bit 63.

## SETTLED PREMISES (do not re-derive; challenge only with evidence)

* Both detectors drive real `rlwimi`/`rldimi` instructions on the unmodified in-tree machine
  `-E bareppc -M 64` (PPC970, 64-bit) through the debugger, one instruction per destination register.
* A 32-bit CPU build (PPC603) keeps only the low word; a 64-bit CPU in 32-bit MODE is disclosed, not
  covered (filed separately as `ppccr0modewidth`).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ppcrldimimask -- RUNG-3 DETECTOR for X(rldimi) mask bounds and wrapping defects.

DEFECT.  src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c, X(rldimi):

    uint32_t iw = ic->arg[0];
    int rs = (iw >> 21) & 31, ra = (iw >> 16) & 31;
    int sh = ((iw >> 11) & 31) | ((iw & 2) << 4);
    int mb = ((iw >> 6) & 31) | (iw & 0x20);
    int rc = ic->arg[0] & 1;
    int m;
    uint64_t tmp, s = cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[rs];
    while (sh-- != 0) { ... }
    m = mb; tmp = 0;
    do {
        tmp |= ((uint64_t)1 << (63-m));
        m ++;
    } while (m != 63 - sh);
    cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[ra] &= ~tmp;
    cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[ra] |= (tmp & s);

THE DEFECT HAS TWO DIRECTIONS:
  (1) The rotate loop `while (sh-- != 0)` post-decrements, leaving `sh == -1` on exit
      for every SH (including SH=0).
  (2) The termination test `m != 63 - sh` is therefore evaluated with `sh == -1`,
      becoming `m != 64` always. The mask generated is always MB..63 instead of MB..63-SH.

  Consequences on two classes of encodings:
  - Non-wrapping (MB <= 63-SH): the mask fails to stop at 63-SH and runs all the way
    to 63, OVERWRITING the low SH bits of destination RA that must be preserved.
  - Wrapping (MB > 63-SH): the mask stops at bit 63 and OMITS the required insertion
    into positions 0..63-SH, leaving those destination bits unchanged.

THE FOUR-EDIT REPAIR:
  1. Save SH in a separate variable: `int m, n = sh;`
  2. Consume the copy in the rotate loop: `while (n-- != 0)`
  3. Circular increment in the mask loop: `m = (m + 1) & 63;`
  4. Compare against successor modulo 64: `while (m != ((64 - sh) & 63));`

A partial repair saving SH but using non-wrapping `m++` and `m != 64 - sh` hits
`(uint64_t)1 << -1` at MB=40, SH=40 (undefined behaviour in C).

ARCHITECTURE, PowerPC Book I v2.01:4315-4327 (rldimi RTL and prose):
  n  <- sh[5] || sh[0:4]
  r  <- ROTL64((RS), n)
  b  <- mb[5] || mb[0:4]
  m  <- MASK(b, ~n)               where ~n on 6-bit field is 63-SH
  RA <- (r & m) | ((RA) & ~m)

  MASK(x, y) is defined at Book I:578 as "1s in positions x through y (wrapping if x > y)".
  PEM:6882 and Book I:4031 confirm "It is not possible to specify an all-zero mask."

CLAUSE (e) DISCLOSURE (what this instrument cannot see):
  (1) Model width vs mode width: the probe runs on `-E bareppc -M 64` (PPC970, 64-bit
      model, MSR[SF]=1). It cannot observe a 64-bit CPU operating in 32-bit mode (MSR[SF]=0),
      where `update_cr0` branching on `cpu->cd.ppc.bits == 64` would compare 64 bits instead
      of 32 bits (filed separately as ppccr0modewidth).
  (2) Unimplemented instructions: `rldic` (XO=2), `rldcl` (XO=8), `rldcr` (XO=9) are not
      implemented in the tree's decoder (`goto bad`) and cannot be driven here.
  (3) Full OS boot rigs: no 64-bit PowerPC guest OS boot image exists in the tree; rung 3
      unmodified machine guest execution is the highest achievable rung.

SHIPPED CONTRACT: 27 rows; 495 distinct census cells.  The census uses an all-ones source and
does not test the rotate amount independently of the mask bounds -- the pattern rows do.  The CR
row checks readback PRESENCE only; CR0 value semantics are not covered.  No rlwimi rows here.

Sentinel: PPC_RLDIMI_PROBE_DONE (plus PPC_RLDIMI_RESULT=n/N, PPC_RLDIMI_CONTROL=OK|FAIL)
"""

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

if len(sys.argv) < 2:
    sys.stderr.write("usage: ppc_rldimi_probe.py <gxemul> [label]\n")
    sys.exit(2)

BIN = sys.argv[1]
LABEL = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "local"
#  The loader needs a 4-byte stub; it is private to this run (the witnesses shared one /tmp path).
_TMPDIR = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ppc_rldimi_")
DUMMY = os.path.join(_TMPDIR, "dummy.bin")
open(DUMMY, "wb").write(b"\x00\x00\x00\x00")

CODE = 0x10000
M64 = (1 << 64) - 1
SENT = 0x5A5A5A5A5A5A5A5A        # sentinel pre-seeded into destination registers
RS_ONES = M64                    # all-ones source: makes every mask window observable
RS_VAL = 0xDEADBEEFCAFEF00D      # pattern source
SRC = 3                          # rS is always r3; r3 is never a destination
DESTS = list(range(4, 30))       # r4..r29 -- 26 destinations per session

rows = []


def row(name, got, want, note=""):
    assert name not in [n for n, _ in rows], "DUPLICATE ROW NAME %r" % name
    assert len(name) <= 18, name
    ok = (got == want)
    rows.append((name, ok))
    print("%-19s %-20s %-20s %-46s %s" % (name, str(got), str(want), note,
                                          "ok" if ok else "FAIL"))
    return ok


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- architecture
def rotl64(x, n):
    n &= 63
    return ((x << n) | (x >> (64 - n))) & M64 if n else x & M64


def mask_b_63(b):
    """MASK(b,63), big-endian bit numbering = the low (64-b) bits."""
    assert 0 <= b <= 63
    return (1 << (64 - b)) - 1


def mask_0_e(e):
    """MASK(0,e), big-endian = the high (e+1) bits."""
    assert 0 <= e <= 63
    return (((1 << (e + 1)) - 1) << (63 - e)) & M64


def mask_range(b, e):
    """MASK(b,e), the architecture's own wrapping mask generator (Book I:578, PEM:6879)."""
    assert 0 <= b <= 63 and 0 <= e <= 63
    m = (mask_b_63(b) & mask_0_e(e)) if b <= e else (mask_b_63(b) | mask_0_e(e))
    assert m != 0, "MASK(%d,%d) came out all-zero, which architecture forbids" % (b, e)
    return m


def want_rldimi(rs_val, ra_val, sh, mb):
    """Architectural rldimi result per Book I:4315."""
    m = mask_range(mb, (63 - sh) & 63)
    return (rotl64(rs_val, sh) & m) | (ra_val & (~m & M64))


def want_rldicl(rs_val, sh, mb):
    return rotl64(rs_val, sh) & mask_b_63(mb)


def want_rldicr(rs_val, sh, me):
    return rotl64(rs_val, sh) & mask_0_e(me)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------- encodings
def enc_md(xo, rs, ra, sh, mbe, rc=0):
    """opcode 30 (rldicl/rldicr/rldimi). Book I format MD."""
    assert 0 <= sh <= 63 and 0 <= mbe <= 63 and 0 <= xo <= 7
    return ((30 << 26) | (rs << 21) | (ra << 16) | ((sh & 31) << 11)
            | ((mbe & 31) << 6) | (((mbe >> 5) & 1) << 5) | (xo << 2)
            | (((sh >> 5) & 1) << 1) | rc) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def RLDICL(ra, rs, sh, mb, rc=0):
    return enc_md(0, rs, ra, sh, mb, rc)


def RLDICR(ra, rs, sh, me, rc=0):
    return enc_md(1, rs, ra, sh, me, rc)


def RLDIMI(ra, rs, sh, mb, rc=0):
    return enc_md(3, rs, ra, sh, mb, rc)


def LI(rd, simm):
    return ((14 << 26) | (rd << 21) | (0 << 16) | (simm & 0xFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def ORI(ra, rs, imm):
    return ((24 << 26) | (rs << 21) | (ra << 16) | (imm & 0xFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF


NOP = ORI(0, 0, 0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- sessions
def session(setup, insns, timeout=90, machine="bareppc", cpu=None):
    """Place `insns' at CODE, seed registers, step exactly len(insns), dump regs."""
    cmds = list(setup)
    for i, w in enumerate(insns):
        cmds.append("put w 0x%x, 0x%08x" % (CODE + 4 * i, w))
    if insns:
        cmds.append("unassemble 0x%x 0x%x" % (CODE, CODE + 4 * len(insns)))
    cmds.append("pc=0x%x" % CODE)
    if insns:
        cmds.append("step %d" % len(insns))
    cmds.append("reg")
    argv = [BIN, "-V", "-x", "-E", machine, "-M", "64"]
    if cpu:
        argv += ["-C", cpu]
    argv += ["0x%x:%s" % (CODE, DUMMY)]
    inp = ("\n".join(cmds + ["quit"]) + "\n").encode("latin-1")
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(argv, input=inp, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                           stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        out = (e.output or b"").decode("latin-1", "replace").replace("\r", "")
        return {}, [], out, "TIMEOUT"
    t = p.stdout.decode("latin-1", "replace").replace("\r", "")
    rc = p.returncode
    how = ("sig%d" % -rc) if rc < 0 else ("exit%d" % rc)
    idx = t.rfind("GXemul> reg")
    regs = {}
    if idx >= 0:
        for m in re.finditer(r"\br(\d\d) = (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)", t[idx:]):
            regs[int(m.group(1))] = int(m.group(2), 16)
        m_cr = re.search(r"\bcr\s*=\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)", t[idx:])
        if m_cr:
            regs["cr"] = int(m_cr.group(1), 16)
    dis = []
    di = t.find("GXemul> unassemble")
    if di >= 0:
        seg = t[di:t.find("GXemul> pc=", di) if t.find("GXemul> pc=", di) > 0
                else len(t)]
        for m in re.finditer(r"^[0-9a-f]{16}: ([0-9a-f]{8})\s*(?:<- )?(\S+)"
                             r"(?:\t(\S+))?", seg, re.M):
            dis.append((int(m.group(1), 16), m.group(2), m.group(3) or ""))
    return regs, dis, t, how


def seed(pairs):
    return ["r%d=0x%x" % (r, v) for r, v in pairs]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ppcrlwimiwidth -- RUNG-3 DETECTOR for X(rlwimi) width contamination and high-half insertion defects.

DEFECT.  src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c, X(rlwimi):

    MODE_uint_t tmp = reg(ic->arg[0]), ra = reg(ic->arg[1]);
    uint32_t iword = ic->arg[2];
    int sh = (iword >> 11) & 31;
    int mb = (iword >> 6) & 31;
    int me = (iword >> 1) & 31;
    int rc = iword & 1;

    tmp = sh ? ((tmp << sh) | (tmp >> (32-sh))) : tmp;

    for (;;) {
        uint64_t mask;
        mask = (uint64_t)1 << (31-mb);
        ra &= ~mask;
        ra |= (tmp & mask);
        if (mb == me)
            break;
        mb ++;
        if (mb == 32)
            mb = 0;
    }
    reg(ic->arg[1]) = ra;
    if (rc)
        update_cr0(cpu, ra);

THE DEFECT HAS TWO PARTS:
  (1) WIDTH CONTAMINATION:
      In 64-bit compilation, MODE_uint_t is uint64_t. When 1 <= SH <= 31,
      `tmp >> (32-sh)` performs a 64-bit right shift, pulling high-half source
      bits down into positions 0..31 of tmp, contaminating the rotated word.
      Siblings rlwinm and rlwnm cast to uint32_t first; rlwimi failed to do so.
  (2) MISSING HIGH-HALF INSERTION:
      ROTL32 rotates the low word duplicated into both halves (positions 0:31
      and 32:63). The architectural mask is MASK(MB+32, ME+32). When MB > ME,
      the mask wraps from bit 63 to bit 0, covering every bit position in 0..31
      (the entire high half). Therefore, when MB > ME, RA's high 32 bits MUST
      be replaced with the rotated low-word data. The unpatched code left the
      high half of RA untouched.

THE TWO-PART REPAIR:
  1. Narrow tmp on read:
     uint32_t tmp = (uint32_t)reg(ic->arg[0]);
  2. High-half replacement before the walk loop:
     if (mb > me)
         ra = (ra & 0xffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)tmp << 32);

  *** THE CONDITIONAL MUST PRECEDE THE LOOP. *** The loop walks mb around to me,
  so after it mb == me and the guard would never fire.

ARCHITECTURE, PowerPC Book I v2.01:4310-4327 (rlwimi RTL and prose):
  n  <- SH
  r  <- ROTL32((RS)[32:63], n)
  m  <- MASK(MB+32, ME+32)
  RA <- (r & m) | ((RA) & ~m)

  MASK(x, y) is defined at Book I:578 as "1s in positions x through y (wrapping if x > y)".
  ROTL32 is defined at Book I:4008 / 4126 as rotating bits 32:63 duplicated into both halves.

CLAUSE (e) DISCLOSURE (what this instrument cannot see):
  (1) Model width vs mode width: the probe runs on `-E bareppc -M 64` (PPC970, 64-bit
      model, MSR[SF]=1). It cannot observe a 64-bit CPU operating in 32-bit mode (MSR[SF]=0),
      where `update_cr0` branching on `cpu->cd.ppc.bits == 64` compares 64 bits instead of
      32 bits (filed separately as ppccr0modewidth).
  (2) 32-bit CPU high-half truncation: on 32-bit CPUs (PPC603), registers are 32 bits, so
      high-half insertion is discarded by 32-bit register truncation.
  (3) Full OS boot rigs: no 64-bit PowerPC guest OS boot image exists in the tree; rung 3
      unmodified machine guest execution is the highest achievable rung.

Sentinel: PPC_RLWIMI_PROBE_DONE (plus PPC_RLWIMI_RESULT=n/N, PPC_RLWIMI_CONTROL=OK|FAIL)

import re
import subprocess

if len(sys.argv) < 2:
    sys.stderr.write("usage: ppc_rlwimi_probe.py <gxemul> [label]\n")
    sys.exit(2)

LABEL = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "local"
#  The loader needs a 4-byte stub; it is private to this run (the witness shared
#  /tmp/ppc_rldimi_dummy.bin with the rldimi witness, so two concurrent runs raced on it).
_TMPDIR = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ppc_rlwimi_")
DUMMY = os.path.join(_TMPDIR, "dummy.bin")
open(DUMMY, "wb").write(b"\x00\x00\x00\x00")

CODE = 0x10000
M64 = (1 << 64) - 1
SENT = 0x5A5A5A5A5A5A5A5A        # sentinel pre-seeded into destination registers
RS_ONES = M64                    # all-ones source
RS_VAL = 0xDEADBEEFCAFEF00D      # pattern source with differing halves
SRC = 3                          # rS is always r3; r3 is never a destination
DESTS = list(range(4, 30))       # r4..r29 -- 26 destinations per session

rows = []


def row(name, got, want, note=""):
    assert name not in [n for n, _ in rows], "DUPLICATE ROW NAME %r" % name
    assert len(name) <= 18, name
    ok = (got == want)
    rows.append((name, ok))
    print("%-19s %-20s %-20s %-46s %s" % (name, str(got), str(want), note,
                                          "ok" if ok else "FAIL"))
    return ok


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- architecture
def rotl64(x, n):
    n &= 63
    return ((x << n) | (x >> (64 - n))) & M64 if n else x & M64


def mask_b_63(b):
    """MASK(b,63), big-endian bit numbering = the low (64-b) bits."""
    assert 0 <= b <= 63
    return (1 << (64 - b)) - 1


def mask_0_e(e):
    """MASK(0,e), big-endian = the high (e+1) bits."""
    assert 0 <= e <= 63
    return (((1 << (e + 1)) - 1) << (63 - e)) & M64


def mask_range(b, e):
    """MASK(b,e), the architecture's own wrapping mask generator (Book I:578, PEM:6879)."""
    assert 0 <= b <= 63 and 0 <= e <= 63
    m = (mask_b_63(b) & mask_0_e(e)) if b <= e else (mask_b_63(b) | mask_0_e(e))
    assert m != 0, "MASK(%d,%d) came out all-zero, which architecture forbids" % (b, e)
    return m


def rotl32(x, n):
    """ROTL[32] per Book I:4008 -- two copies of (RS)[32:63], then rotate."""
    lo = x & 0xFFFFFFFF
    n &= 31
    r32 = ((lo << n) | (lo >> (32 - n))) & 0xFFFFFFFF if n else lo
    return (r32 << 32) | r32


def mask32(mb, me):
    """MASK(MB+32, ME+32) at 64 bits (Book I:4125, 4310)."""
    assert 0 <= mb <= 31 and 0 <= me <= 31
    return mask_range(mb + 32, me + 32)


def want_rlwimi(rs_val, ra_val, sh, mb, me):
    """Architectural rlwimi result per Book I:4310."""
    m = mask32(mb, me)
    return (rotl32(rs_val, sh) & m) | (ra_val & (~m & M64))


def want_rlwinm(rs_val, sh, mb, me):
    """Architectural rlwinm result per Book I:4125."""
    m = mask32(mb, me)
    return rotl32(rs_val, sh) & m


# -------------------------------------------------------------------- encodings
def enc_m(op, rs, ra, sh, mb, me, rc=0):
    """Opcode 20 (rlwimi) / 21 (rlwinm) / 23 (rlwnm). Book I format M."""
    assert 0 <= op <= 63 and 0 <= rs <= 31 and 0 <= ra <= 31
    assert 0 <= sh <= 31 and 0 <= mb <= 31 and 0 <= me <= 31 and 0 <= rc <= 1
    return ((op << 26) | (rs << 21) | (ra << 16) | (sh << 11)
            | (mb << 6) | (me << 1) | rc) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def RLWIMI(ra, rs, sh, mb, me, rc=0):
    return enc_m(20, rs, ra, sh, mb, me, rc)


def RLWINM(ra, rs, sh, mb, me, rc=0):
    return enc_m(21, rs, ra, sh, mb, me, rc)


def LI(rd, simm):
    return ((14 << 26) | (rd << 21) | (0 << 16) | (simm & 0xFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def ORI(ra, rs, imm):
    return ((24 << 26) | (rs << 21) | (ra << 16) | (imm & 0xFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF


NOP = ORI(0, 0, 0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- sessions
def session(setup, insns, timeout=90, machine="bareppc", cpu=None):
    """Place `insns' at CODE, seed registers, step exactly len(insns), dump regs."""
    cmds = list(setup)
    for i, w in enumerate(insns):
        cmds.append("put w 0x%x, 0x%08x" % (CODE + 4 * i, w))
    if insns:
        cmds.append("unassemble 0x%x 0x%x" % (CODE, CODE + 4 * len(insns)))
    cmds.append("pc=0x%x" % CODE)
    if insns:
        cmds.append("step %d" % len(insns))
    cmds.append("reg")
    argv = [BIN, "-V", "-x", "-E", machine, "-M", "64"]
    if cpu:
        argv += ["-C", cpu]
    argv += ["0x%x:%s" % (CODE, DUMMY)]
    inp = ("\n".join(cmds + ["quit"]) + "\n").encode("latin-1")
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(argv, input=inp, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                           stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        out = (e.output or b"").decode("latin-1", "replace").replace("\r", "")
        return {}, [], out, "TIMEOUT"
    t = p.stdout.decode("latin-1", "replace").replace("\r", "")
    rc = p.returncode
    how = ("sig%d" % -rc) if rc < 0 else ("exit%d" % rc)
    idx = t.rfind("GXemul> reg")
    regs = {}
    if idx >= 0:
        for m in re.finditer(r"\br(\d\d) = (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)", t[idx:]):
            regs[int(m.group(1))] = int(m.group(2), 16)
        m_cr = re.search(r"\bcr\s*=\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)", t[idx:])
        if m_cr:
            regs["cr"] = int(m_cr.group(1), 16)
    dis = []
    di = t.find("GXemul> unassemble")
    if di >= 0:
        seg = t[di:t.find("GXemul> pc=", di) if t.find("GXemul> pc=", di) > 0
                else len(t)]
        for m in re.finditer(r"^[0-9a-f]{16}: ([0-9a-f]{8})\s*(?:<- )?(\S+)"
                             r"(?:\t(\S+))?", seg, re.M):
            dis.append((int(m.group(1), 16), m.group(2), m.group(3) or ""))
    return regs, dis, t, how


def seed(pairs):
    return ["r%d=0x%x" % (r, v) for r, v in pairs]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ppcrldimimask -- RUNG-3 DETECTOR for X(rldimi) mask bounds and wrapping defects.

DEFECT.  src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c, X(rldimi):

    uint32_t iw = ic->arg[0];
    int rs = (iw >> 21) & 31, ra = (iw >> 16) & 31;
    int sh = ((iw >> 11) & 31) | ((iw & 2) << 4);
    int mb = ((iw >> 6) & 31) | (iw & 0x20);
    int rc = ic->arg[0] & 1;
    int m;
    uint64_t tmp, s = cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[rs];
    while (sh-- != 0) { ... }
    m = mb; tmp = 0;
    do {
        tmp |= ((uint64_t)1 << (63-m));
        m ++;
    } while (m != 63 - sh);
    cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[ra] &= ~tmp;
    cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[ra] |= (tmp & s);

THE DEFECT HAS TWO DIRECTIONS:
  (1) The rotate loop `while (sh-- != 0)` post-decrements, leaving `sh == -1` on exit
      for every SH (including SH=0).
  (2) The termination test `m != 63 - sh` is therefore evaluated with `sh == -1`,
      becoming `m != 64` always. The mask generated is always MB..63 instead of MB..63-SH.

  Consequences on two classes of encodings:
  - Non-wrapping (MB <= 63-SH): the mask fails to stop at 63-SH and runs all the way
    to 63, OVERWRITING the low SH bits of destination RA that must be preserved.
  - Wrapping (MB > 63-SH): the mask stops at bit 63 and OMITS the required insertion
    into positions 0..63-SH, leaving those destination bits unchanged.

THE FOUR-EDIT REPAIR:
  1. Save SH in a separate variable: `int m, n = sh;`
  2. Consume the copy in the rotate loop: `while (n-- != 0)`
  3. Circular increment in the mask loop: `m = (m + 1) & 63;`
  4. Compare against successor modulo 64: `while (m != ((64 - sh) & 63));`

A partial repair saving SH but using non-wrapping `m++` and `m != 64 - sh` hits
`(uint64_t)1 << -1` at MB=40, SH=40 (undefined behaviour in C).

ARCHITECTURE, PowerPC Book I v2.01:4315-4327 (rldimi RTL and prose):
  n  <- sh[5] || sh[0:4]
  r  <- ROTL64((RS), n)
  b  <- mb[5] || mb[0:4]
  m  <- MASK(b, ~n)               where ~n on 6-bit field is 63-SH
  RA <- (r & m) | ((RA) & ~m)

  MASK(x, y) is defined at Book I:578 as "1s in positions x through y (wrapping if x > y)".
  PEM:6882 and Book I:4031 confirm "It is not possible to specify an all-zero mask."

CLAUSE (e) DISCLOSURE (what this instrument cannot see):
  (1) Model width vs mode width: the probe runs on `-E bareppc -M 64` (PPC970, 64-bit
      model, MSR[SF]=1). It cannot observe a 64-bit CPU operating in 32-bit mode (MSR[SF]=0),
      where `update_cr0` branching on `cpu->cd.ppc.bits == 64` would compare 64 bits instead
      of 32 bits (filed separately as ppccr0modewidth).
  (2) Unimplemented instructions: `rldic` (XO=2), `rldcl` (XO=8), `rldcr` (XO=9) are not
      implemented in the tree's decoder (`goto bad`) and cannot be driven here.
  (3) Full OS boot rigs: no 64-bit PowerPC guest OS boot image exists in the tree; rung 3
      unmodified machine guest execution is the highest achievable rung.

SHIPPED CONTRACT: 27 rows; 495 distinct census cells.  The census uses an all-ones source and
does not test the rotate amount independently of the mask bounds -- the pattern rows do.  The CR
row checks readback PRESENCE only; CR0 value semantics are not covered.  No rlwimi rows here.

Sentinel: PPC_RLDIMI_PROBE_DONE (plus PPC_RLDIMI_RESULT=n/N, PPC_RLDIMI_CONTROL=OK|FAIL)
"""

import os

import sys
import tempfile
import time

if len(sys.argv) < 2:
    sys.stderr.write("usage: ppc_rldimi_probe.py <gxemul> [label]\n")
    sys.exit(2)

BIN = sys.argv[1]
LABEL = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "local"
#  The loader needs a 4-byte stub; it is private to this run (the witnesses shared one /tmp path).
_TMPDIR = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ppc_rldimi_")
DUMMY = os.path.join(_TMPDIR, "dummy.bin")
open(DUMMY, "wb").write(b"\x00\x00\x00\x00")

CODE = 0x10000
M64 = (1 << 64) - 1
SENT = 0x5A5A5A5A5A5A5A5A        # sentinel pre-seeded into destination registers
RS_ONES = M64                    # all-ones source: makes every mask window observable
RS_VAL = 0xDEADBEEFCAFEF00D      # pattern source
SRC = 3                          # rS is always r3; r3 is never a destination
DESTS = list(range(4, 30))       # r4..r29 -- 26 destinations per session

rows = []


def row(name, got, want, note=""):
    assert name not in [n for n, _ in rows], "DUPLICATE ROW NAME %r" % name
    assert len(name) <= 18, name
    ok = (got == want)
    rows.append((name, ok))
    print("%-19s %-20s %-20s %-46s %s" % (name, str(got), str(want), note,
                                          "ok" if ok else "FAIL"))
    return ok


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- architecture
def rotl64(x, n):
    n &= 63
    return ((x << n) | (x >> (64 - n))) & M64 if n else x & M64


def mask_b_63(b):
    """MASK(b,63), big-endian bit numbering = the low (64-b) bits."""
    assert 0 <= b <= 63
    return (1 << (64 - b)) - 1


def mask_0_e(e):
    """MASK(0,e), big-endian = the high (e+1) bits."""
    assert 0 <= e <= 63
    return (((1 << (e + 1)) - 1) << (63 - e)) & M64


def mask_range(b, e):
    """MASK(b,e), the architecture's own wrapping mask generator (Book I:578, PEM:6879)."""
    assert 0 <= b <= 63 and 0 <= e <= 63
    m = (mask_b_63(b) & mask_0_e(e)) if b <= e else (mask_b_63(b) | mask_0_e(e))
    assert m != 0, "MASK(%d,%d) came out all-zero, which architecture forbids" % (b, e)
    return m


def want_rldimi(rs_val, ra_val, sh, mb):
    """Architectural rldimi result per Book I:4315."""
    m = mask_range(mb, (63 - sh) & 63)
    return (rotl64(rs_val, sh) & m) | (ra_val & (~m & M64))


def want_rldicl(rs_val, sh, mb):
    return rotl64(rs_val, sh) & mask_b_63(mb)


def want_rldicr(rs_val, sh, me):
    return rotl64(rs_val, sh) & mask_0_e(me)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------- encodings
def enc_md(xo, rs, ra, sh, mbe, rc=0):
    """opcode 30 (rldicl/rldicr/rldimi). Book I format MD."""
    assert 0 <= sh <= 63 and 0 <= mbe <= 63 and 0 <= xo <= 7
    return ((30 << 26) | (rs << 21) | (ra << 16) | ((sh & 31) << 11)
            | ((mbe & 31) << 6) | (((mbe >> 5) & 1) << 5) | (xo << 2)
            | (((sh >> 5) & 1) << 1) | rc) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def RLDICL(ra, rs, sh, mb, rc=0):
    return enc_md(0, rs, ra, sh, mb, rc)


def RLDICR(ra, rs, sh, me, rc=0):
    return enc_md(1, rs, ra, sh, me, rc)


def RLDIMI(ra, rs, sh, mb, rc=0):
    return enc_md(3, rs, ra, sh, mb, rc)


def LI(rd, simm):
    return ((14 << 26) | (rd << 21) | (0 << 16) | (simm & 0xFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def ORI(ra, rs, imm):
    return ((24 << 26) | (rs << 21) | (ra << 16) | (imm & 0xFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF


NOP = ORI(0, 0, 0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- sessions
def session(setup, insns, timeout=90, machine="bareppc", cpu=None):
    """Place `insns' at CODE, seed registers, step exactly len(insns), dump regs."""
    cmds = list(setup)
    for i, w in enumerate(insns):
        cmds.append("put w 0x%x, 0x%08x" % (CODE + 4 * i, w))
    if insns:
        cmds.append("unassemble 0x%x 0x%x" % (CODE, CODE + 4 * len(insns)))
    cmds.append("pc=0x%x" % CODE)
    if insns:
        cmds.append("step %d" % len(insns))
    cmds.append("reg")
    argv = [BIN, "-V", "-x", "-E", machine, "-M", "64"]
    if cpu:
        argv += ["-C", cpu]
    argv += ["0x%x:%s" % (CODE, DUMMY)]
    inp = ("\n".join(cmds + ["quit"]) + "\n").encode("latin-1")
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(argv, input=inp, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                           stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        out = (e.output or b"").decode("latin-1", "replace").replace("\r", "")
        return {}, [], out, "TIMEOUT"
    t = p.stdout.decode("latin-1", "replace").replace("\r", "")
    rc = p.returncode
    how = ("sig%d" % -rc) if rc < 0 else ("exit%d" % rc)
    idx = t.rfind("GXemul> reg")
    regs = {}
    if idx >= 0:
        for m in re.finditer(r"\br(\d\d) = (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)", t[idx:]):
            regs[int(m.group(1))] = int(m.group(2), 16)
        m_cr = re.search(r"\bcr\s*=\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)", t[idx:])
        if m_cr:
            regs["cr"] = int(m_cr.group(1), 16)
    dis = []
    di = t.find("GXemul> unassemble")
    if di >= 0:
        seg = t[di:t.find("GXemul> pc=", di) if t.find("GXemul> pc=", di) > 0
                else len(t)]
        for m in re.finditer(r"^[0-9a-f]{16}: ([0-9a-f]{8})\s*(?:<- )?(\S+)"
                             r"(?:\t(\S+))?", seg, re.M):
            dis.append((int(m.group(1), 16), m.group(2), m.group(3) or ""))
    return regs, dis, t, how


def seed(pairs):
    return ["r%d=0x%x" % (r, v) for r, v in pairs]


print("ppcrldimimask RUNG-3 DETECTOR -- binary=%s label=%s" % (BIN, LABEL))
print("machine: -E bareppc -M 64 (UNMODIFIED in-tree; MACHINE_DEFAULT_CPU=PPC970, 64-bit)")
print("wants derived from PowerPC Book I v2.01:4315 (rldimi)")
print("%-19s %-20s %-20s %-46s %s" % ("row", "got", "want", "note", ""))
t0 = time.time()
disasm_checked = 0
disasm_ok = 0

# ============================================================ CONTROL SESSION ==
ctl_insns = [
    LI(9, 0x1234),                       # liveness
    NOP,                                 # seed-holds probe steps over this
    RLDICL(4, SRC, 0, 32),               # clrldi r4,r3,32 -- sibling control
    RLDICR(5, SRC, 0, 31),               # sibling control
]
ctl_setup = seed([(SRC, RS_VAL), (30, SENT)] + [(r, SENT) for r in DESTS])
regs, dis, T, how = session(ctl_setup, ctl_insns)

row("session", how, "exit0", "the control session ran to `quit'")
row("live", hex(regs.get(9, -1)), hex(0x1234),
    "li r9,0x1234 -- guest executes and readback works")
row("seed holds", hex(regs.get(30, -1)), hex(SENT),
    "r30 seeded, never destination: proves write is real")
row("src intact", hex(regs.get(SRC, -1)), hex(RS_VAL),
    "rS is unchanged by instructions")

want_dis = ["li", "nop", "rldicl", "rldicr"]
want_ops = ["r9,4660", "", "r4,r3,0,32", "r5,r3,0,31"]
got_pairs = [(m, o) for _, m, o in dis]
disasm_checked += len(want_dis)
disasm_ok += sum(1 for i, (m, o) in enumerate(got_pairs[:len(want_dis)])
                 if m == want_dis[i] and o == want_ops[i])
row("disasm xcheck", "%d/%d" % (disasm_ok, disasm_checked), "4/4",
    "tree's disassembler agrees with encoder")
row("ctl rldicl", hex(regs.get(4, -1)), hex(want_rldicl(RS_VAL, 0, 32)),
    "sibling control: rldicl zero-extend")
row("ctl rldicr", hex(regs.get(5, -1)), hex(want_rldicr(RS_VAL, 0, 31)),
    "sibling control: rldicr extract")

# ================================================ NEGATIVE APPARATUS CONTROL ==

# ============================================ REACHABILITY CONTROL (32-bit) ===

# Session 1: Non-wrapping encodings (MB <= 63-SH), rA initialized to 0, rS = ~0
# Defect symptom: overwrites low SH bits (runs to bit 63 instead of 63-SH)

    RLDIMI(5, SRC, 32, 0),       # SH=32, MB=0 -> mask 0..31; defect gives 0..63
    RLDIMI(6, SRC, 0, 0),        # SH=0, MB=0 -> mask 0..63 (coincidental agree)
    RLDIMI(7, SRC, 16, 16),      # SH=16, MB=16 -> mask 16..47; defect gives 16..63
    RLDIMI(8, SRC, 0, 63),       # SH=0, MB=63 -> mask 63..63 (singleton bit 63)

# Session 2: Wrapping encodings (MB > 63-SH), rA initialized to 0, rS = ~0
# Defect symptom: stops at bit 63 and OMITS insertion into positions 0..63-SH
s2_setup = seed([(SRC, RS_ONES)] + [(r, 0) for r in DESTS])
s2_insns = [
    RLDIMI(4, SRC, 40, 40),      # SH=40, MB=40 -> 63-SH=23; mask 40..63 + 0..23 (48 bits)
    RLDIMI(5, SRC, 63, 63),      # SH=63, MB=63 -> 63-SH=0; mask 63 + 0 (2 bits)
    RLDIMI(6, SRC, 63, 1),       # SH=63, MB=1 -> 63-SH=0; mask 1..63 + 0 (64 bits, full)
    RLDIMI(7, SRC, 48, 32),      # SH=48, MB=32 -> 63-SH=15; mask 32..63 + 0..15 (48 bits)

# Session 3: Destination preservation with structured data and seeded rA
s3_setup = seed([(SRC, RS_VAL)] + [(r, SENT) for r in DESTS])

# ==================================================== COMPREHENSIVE CENSUS =====
# Sweep structured combinations across the full (SH, MB) space:
# - MB sweeps at fixed SH in {0, 8, 40, 63} (4 x 64 = 256)
# - SH sweeps at fixed MB in {0, 40} (2 x 64 = 128)
# - Diagonal (k, k) for k in 0..63 (64)
# - Anti-diagonal (k, 63-k) for k in 0..63 (64)
census_combos = []
for sh_val in [0, 8, 40, 63]:
    for mb_val in range(64):
        census_combos.append((sh_val, mb_val))
for mb_val in [0, 40]:
    for sh_val in range(64):
        census_combos.append((sh_val, mb_val))
for k in range(64):
    census_combos.append((k, k))
    census_combos.append((k, (63 - k) & 63))

seen = set()
uniq_census = []
for c in census_combos:
    if c not in seen:
        seen.add(c)
        uniq_census.append(c)

census_fail = 0

for base in range(0, len(uniq_census), len(DESTS)):

            disasm_ok += 1

1318-> **COST: one mutant per repair predicate**, the same order as the accept-row rule (#448 = 4,
1319-> #449 = 1, #461 = 4 across two arms). It is bounded by the diff, so it cannot become #392:
1320-> the predicates are the ones the fix ADDED, and that list is finite and visible.
1321->
1322-> ### *** "THE PREDICATE THE FIX INTRODUCED" ENUMERATED THE EMPTY SET FOR MOST OF THIS
1323:> ### QUEUE, AND NOBODY NOTICED FOR THREE ROUNDS. Corrected 2026-08-24 -- clause (d) now
1324-> ### reads DEPENDS ON, not INTRODUCED. ***
1325->
1326:> Clause (d) says *keep the guard, null its repair*. As written it enumerated only
1327-> predicates the diff ADDS -- and **the two commonest fix shapes here add none**:
1328->
1329-> * a **pure deletion** introduces no predicate at all;
1330-> * a **DE-FATALISATION** introduces none either -- it changes what an EXISTING
1331->   predicate's branch does. That is most of this project's queue.
1332->
1333:> So for those rounds clause (d) enumerated **nothing**, and a round could satisfy the
1334:> floor while having built no (d) mutant whatever. `#461` measured (d) successfully only
1335-> because its fix happened to ADD a predicate (an alignment mask) for the mutant to weaken.
1336->
1337-> **Reading it as DEPENDS ON fixes both cases at once**, and it is why this now replaces a
1338-> narrower deletion-only rule written earlier the same day: that rule was a special case of
1339-> this gap, and two overlapping statements of one rule is the accumulation this carrier is
1340-> supposed to refuse.
1341->
1342-> **The two shapes, once the enumeration is right:**
1343-> * **fix ADDS a predicate** -> weaken the added one (unchanged; the original rule).
1344:> * **fix adds none** -> the (d) mutant reroutes an EXISTING guard's repair. For a
1345->   de-fatalisation: **swap the guard's operand for a field the guarded BODY reads.**
1346->   For a pure deletion: **re-introduce the removed behaviour under a DIFFERENT predicate**
1347:>   -- not the same one widened, which is (b) wearing (d)'s clothes.
1348->
1349-> *** THE MEASURED CASE, and it is why this matters rather than being tidy: ***
1350-> `#462` de-fatalised two arms. Its guard reads `d->data`; the body it guards reads
1351-> `d->data` AND `d->data_len`; the two are set together in one place and cleared in two
1352-> places that touch only ONE of them. Swapping the guard's operand to `d->data_len == 0`
1353-> **scored a CLEAN SWEEP on a 52-row detector that had just passed twelve mutants**, and
1354-> restored a NULL-pointer read of 408 bytes. Under the old wording that was coverage debt;
1355-> under DEPENDS ON it is a **floor breach, L2, fix in-round** -- which is what the round
1356-> did, before the wording was corrected.

1359-> #### CHASING, which is unbounded and is how this becomes `#392`. Named 2026-08-24 by the
1360-> #### adjudicating seat, in the same breath as upholding the correction. ***
1361->
1362-> > **DEPENDS ON enumerates exactly two things: (1) the predicates DOMINATING the diff's
1363-> > edited lines, walked up only to the ENCLOSING FUNCTION BOUNDARY -- never into callees
1364-> > or callers; and (2) for operand-swap forms, swaps drawn ONLY from fields the guarded
1365-> > BODY reads (the guard-field/body-field grep the pre-table check already mandates).**

1369-> `data_len` is a body-read field (clause 2), so `M11` falls out mechanically rather than
1370-> by inspiration. It cannot become `#392` because the enumeration stays closed over the
1371-> diff's own hunks -- the same closure the INTRODUCED wording had, without the empty-set
1372-> defect that made INTRODUCED enumerate nothing for a de-fatalisation.

1393-> value space is 2^32 apiece, so "finite" does no bounding work on its motivating case (a C `int` is
1394-> finite -- the first wording here said it was not; codex and glm caught it on pass 11); "reachable
1395-> guest state" would force rowing

1638-> #### AND THE OBVIOUS GENERALISATION IS UNBOUNDED, SO IT IS NOT THE ONE ADOPTED
1639->
1640-> The tempting sentence is *"every VALUE and every STATE in which a guard refuses needs a
1641-> decline-channel row."*  **That licenses unbounded row growth -- the `#392` shape** -- and the
1642-> adjudication that produced this line rejected it for exactly that reason. The distinction:
1643->
1644-> * **ROW DEMAND** -- *which* refusals need pinning -- is ALREADY bounded and is not touched:
1645:>   the floor clauses, the (d) DEPENDS-ON closure, one accept row per conditioned predicate,
1646->   one anchor row per position claim, one ask-again. **Rows are owed PER ENUMERATED MUTANT,
1647->   never per refusing state**; two states no enumerated mutant distinguishes collapse into one
1648->   row. That enumeration is diff-closed and finite.
1649-> * **ROW VALIDITY** -- what `#489` actually measured -- is the CHANNEL line above, and it is a
1650->   WRITE-TIME check on rows that already exist.
1651->
1652-> > **A FILTER CAN REJECT OR REPAIR A ROW; IT CAN NEVER DEMAND A NEW ONE -- SO IT CANNOT GROW
1653-> > WITHOUT BOUND.**  That is the stop condition, and it is structural rather than a cap: the
1654-> > generator side is untouched.
1655->
1656-> *Mechanising it -- a `# kills: <mutant> via <channel>` comment per row -- is FILED, not
1657-> adopted: it changes what every probe in the tree must carry, and that is an owner decision
1658-> rather than a round's.*
1659->
1660-> **The third is the one that looked impossible and is the cheapest.** It only seemed
1661-> unreachable because it was approached from the mutant side -- *"what edit escapes?"*,
1662-> which is unbounded -- instead of the field side -- *"what states can these two fields be
1663-> in?"*, which is a grep. In `#462` that was three lines of output: `alloc_data` sets both
1664-> fields; two `free` sites clear only one.
1665->
1666-> **DO NOT move the ask-again earlier.** It works BECAUSE a clean table redirects seats away
1667-> from shapes the author already covered; measured yield says so. And do not raise the cap

1670-> **(e) THE CONTRACT.** The probe header names which edits this detector is designed

1672-> not* -- and a later escape becomes "outside the contract" or "a breach of it",
1673-> which are different dispositions, rather than an argument about overclaiming.
1674-> Two lines in a header.

1680-> ### *** (f) THE ANCHOR RULE -- adopted 2026-08-25 after a CLEAN 12/12 detector was escaped
1681-> ### by a ONE-TERM translation that three purpose-built rows could not see BY CONSTRUCTION. ***
1682->
1683-> **Rows that assert only PAIRWISE DISTINCTNESS, or a same-path round-trip, test the decode
1684-> against ITSELF.** They are therefore invariant under any edit that re-maps addresses
1685-> INJECTIVELY over the probed set -- translations first among them -- and they catch a re-map
1686-> only where it COLLIDES on that set.
1687->
1688-> `#463` shipped three rows built specifically to pin an index bound: `alias`, `alias2` and
1689-> `crossarr`. All three read back `+0x10` and together assert exactly
1690-> `cell(+0x10) != cell(+0x14), cell(+0x18), cell(+0x24)`. **They never assert WHICH cell any
1691-> offset names.** So `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` -> `((relative_addr / 4) + 1) & 3` slid the
1692-> whole window one word, every pair stayed distinct, and the detector scored a CLEAN SWEEP --
1693-> while every `+0x?8` register moved one past a `[3]` array and a documented register's store
1694-> landed on `int asserted_13`, making the device drop a legitimately pending interrupt.

2301-> ### *** THE ORACLE-CORRECTION RULE — adopted 2026-08-22, and it is TEST-FIRST restated
2302-> for the case test-first did not cover. ***
2303->
2304-> Sometimes the DETECTOR is the thing that is wrong: a shipped row pins the opposite of the
2305-> architecture, so correcting the code turns the row red. Re-pinning it is then necessary —
2306-> and it is also **observationally identical to fitting the test to the binary**, which is
2307-> the classic way to fake a green detector.
2308->
2309-> **THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ORDER, AND IT IS MECHANICAL:**
2310->
2311-> > **Re-pin the oracle FIRST. Measure the COMMITTED build RED under the new expectations.
2312-> > THEN change the code.** Same scripts, opposite colour. If you cannot show that red, you
2313-> > do not have test-first, and the re-pin collapses into laundering.

2317->   file/line, so a future seat can re-derive it without trusting this round. The old pin's

2477-> #### THE BOUND IS IMPORTED, NOT INTRINSIC -- state the dependency or the rule overclaims
2478->
2479-> The stop condition does not bound the chain and must not pretend to. The bound comes from
2480:> **the (d) DEPENDS-ON enumeration being diff-closed and finite**, and from *zero breaches*
2481-> meaning **zero SURVIVING ADJUDICATION** rather than zero raised -- otherwise one stubborn
2482-> seat blocks closure forever, against the count-arguments-not-seats rule. With those imports
2483-> the chain is infinite only if every repair is defective, in which case every pass is buying a
2484-> real defect off the ship.
2485->
2486-> #### *** THE AMENDMENT THAT ACTUALLY ENDS CHAINS, and it is the part worth carrying. ***
2487->
2488-> `#499`'s three breaches were **THE SAME CLASS THREE TIMES** -- a cell of one state space left
2489-> empty, repaired at exactly the address the mutant had used, leaving the symmetric cell open
2490-> for the next pass. Pass 1 found *width* unpinned; pass 2 found *component*; pass 3 found
2491-> *direction* AND *position*. **Pass-per-instance converges LINEARLY IN CELLS**, and 28 -> 34
2492-> -> 36 rows bought one cell each.
2493->
2494-> > **WHEN TWO CONSECUTIVE PASSES FIND BREACHES OF ONE CLASS, THE NEXT REPAIR OWES THE CLASS
2495-> > CLOSURE: enumerate the full space from the function's own inputs, close every cell in ONE
2496-> > diff, and write into the CONTRACT which cells are covered and which are deliberately not.
2497-> > The closing pass then VERIFIES THE ENUMERATION rather than hunting cells.**
2498->
2499-> That is the reading-seat-buys-the-class lesson wearing the repair hat. It also converts a
2500-> future escape from *"another breach"* into *"outside the contract, as stated"* -- which is
2501-> exactly what clause (e) is for, and which a cell-by-cell chain can never reach.
2502->

import ast, pathlib, itertools, collections, operator
ROOT=pathlib.Path(r'C:\\DocumentNoSnc\\CC\\GXEMUL\\GXEMUL-SEC')
M64=(1<<64)-1
M32=(1<<32)-1
SENT=0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a
RS=0xdeadbeefcafef00d
def read_probe(fn):
    tree=ast.parse((ROOT/'regress'/fn).read_text())
    env={}
    defs={'rotl64','rotl32','mask_b_63','mask_0_e','mask_range','mask32','want_rlwimi','want_rlwinm','want_rldimi','want_rldicl','want_rldicr'}
    names={'M64','SENT','RS_ONES','RS_VAL','MUT_RS','SRC','DESTS','census_combos','mb_me_nowrap','mb_me_wrap','seen','uniq_census'}
    chosen=[]
    census=False
    for node in tree.body:
        if isinstance(node,ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in defs: chosen.append(node)
        elif isinstance(node,ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t,ast.Name) and t.id in names for t in node.targets):
            chosen.append(node)
            if any(isinstance(t,ast.Name) and t.id=='census_combos' for t in node.targets): census=True
        elif census and isinstance(node,ast.For):
            if isinstance(node.target,ast.Name) and node.target.id=='base': census=False
            else: chosen.append(node)
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=chosen,type_ignores=[]),str(fn),'exec'),env)
    tests=[]
    wanted='want_rlwimi' if 'rlwimi' in fn else 'want_rldimi'
    for node in tree.body:
        if not (isinstance(node,ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value,ast.Call) and isinstance(node.value.func,ast.Name) and node.value.func.id=='row'): continue
        call=node.value
        for sub in ast.walk(call.args[2]):
            if isinstance(sub,ast.Call) and isinstance(sub.func,ast.Name) and sub.func.id==wanted:
                args=tuple(eval(compile(ast.Expression(a),str(fn),'eval'),env) for a in sub.args)
                tests.append((ast.literal_eval(call.args[0]),args,env[wanted](*args)))
    src,dst=(RS,SENT) if wanted=='want_rlwimi' else (M64,0)
    tests += [('census '+str(cell),(src,dst,*cell),env[wanted](src,dst,*cell)) for cell in env['uniq_census']]
    return env,tests
R,RT=read_probe('ppc_rlwimi_probe.py')

OPS={'==':operator.eq,'"'!='"':operator.ne,'>':operator.gt,'>=':operator.ge,'<':operator.lt,'<=':operator.le}
class Bad(Exception): pass
def rm(rs,ra,sh,mb,me,cfg={}):
    tmp=rs&M32
    v=dict(tmp=tmp,ra=ra,sh=sh,mb=mb,me=me)
    if cfg.get('shpred',lambda v:v['sh'])(v):
        if not 1<=sh<=31: raise Bad('UB shift')
        tmp=((tmp<<sh)|(tmp>>(32-sh)))&M32
    v.update(tmp=tmp)
    if cfg.get('highpred',lambda v:v['mb']>v['me'])(v):
        h=cfg.get('highword',lambda v,rs:v['tmp'])(v,rs)
        low=cfg.get('lowpres',lambda v:v['ra'])(v)
        ra=((low&M32)|(h<<32))&M64
    for _ in range(65):
        if not 0<=mb<32: raise Bad('UB shift')
        mask=1<<(31-mb)
        v.update(ra=ra,mb=mb)
        part=cfg.get('insert',lambda v:v['tmp'])(v)
        ra=((ra&~mask)|(part&mask))&M64
        v.update(ra=ra,mb=mb)
        if cfg.get('breakpred',lambda v:v['mb']==v['me'])(v): return ra
        mb+=1
        v.update(mb=mb)
        if cfg.get('resetpred',lambda v:v['mb']==32)(v): mb=0
    raise Bad('loop')
def dm(rs,ra,sh,mb,cfg={}):
    s=rs
    v=dict(sh=sh,mb=mb,ra=ra,s=s)
    n=cfg.get('ninit',lambda v:v['sh'])(v)
    for _ in range(66):
        v.update(n=n,s=s)
        yes=cfg.get('rotpred',lambda v:v['n']"'!=0)(v)
        n-=1
        if not yes: break
        b=cfg.get('"'bit',lambda v:(v['s']>>63)&1)(v)
        s=((s<<1)|b)&M64
    else: raise Bad('loop')
    v.update(n=n,s=s)
    m=cfg.get('mstart',lambda v:v['mb'])(v)
    tmp=0
    for _ in range(65):
        if not 0<=m<64: raise Bad('UB shift')
        tmp|=1<<(63-m)
        v.update(m=m,tmp=tmp)
        m=cfg.get('mstep',lambda v:(v['m']+1)&63)(v)
        v.update(m=m)
        if not cfg.get('endpred',lambda v:v['m']"'!=((64-v['"'sh'])&63))(v):
            return ((ra&~tmp)|(tmp&s))&M64
    raise Bad('loop')
def inspect(model,tests,cfg):
    fails=[]; invalid=[]
    for name,args,want in tests:
        try:
            got=model(*args,cfg)
            if got"'!=want: fails.append((name,hex(got),hex(want)))
        except Bad as e: invalid.append((name,str(e)))
    return dict(fails=len(fails),invalid=len(invalid),first=(fails+invalid)[:3])

]:

I found a rotate-loop survivor in the model: skip rotation when `mb == ((64 - sh) & 63)`, while still building and applying the mask. That condition selects a full-register mask. The detector’s `wrap full` row and matching census cells use all ones, so they hide the missing rotation; none of the three pattern rows exercises it. I’m checking the remaining swaps and the fixes across the full immediate space.

def read_probe(fn):
    tree=ast.parse((ROOT/'regress'/fn).read_text())
    env={}
    defs={'rotl64','rotl32','mask_b_63','mask_0_e','mask_range','mask32','want_rlwimi','want_rlwinm','want_rldimi','want_rldicl','want_rldicr'}
    names={'M64','SENT','RS_ONES','RS_VAL','MUT_RS','SRC','DESTS','census_combos','mb_me_nowrap','mb_me_wrap','seen','uniq_census'}
    chosen=[]
    census=False
    for node in tree.body:
        if isinstance(node,ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in defs: chosen.append(node)
        elif isinstance(node,ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t,ast.Name) and t.id in names for t in node.targets):
            chosen.append(node)
            if any(isinstance(t,ast.Name) and t.id=='census_combos' for t in node.targets): census=True
        elif census and isinstance(node,ast.For):
            if isinstance(node.target,ast.Name) and node.target.id=='base': census=False
            else: chosen.append(node)
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=chosen,type_ignores=[]),str(fn),'exec'),env)
    tests=[]
    wanted='want_rlwimi' if 'rlwimi' in fn else 'want_rldimi'
    for node in tree.body:
        if not (isinstance(node,ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value,ast.Call) and isinstance(node.value.func,ast.Name) and node.value.func.id=='row'): continue
        call=node.value
        for sub in ast.walk(call.args[2]):
            if isinstance(sub,ast.Call) and isinstance(sub.func,ast.Name) and sub.func.id==wanted:
                args=tuple(eval(compile(ast.Expression(a),str(fn),'eval'),env) for a in sub.args)
                tests.append((ast.literal_eval(call.args[0]),args,env[wanted](*args)))
    src,dst=(RS,SENT) if wanted=='want_rlwimi' else (M64,0)
    tests += [('census '+str(cell),(src,dst,*cell),env[wanted](src,dst,*cell)) for cell in env['uniq_census']]
    return env,tests

class Bad(Exception): pass
def rm(rs,ra,sh,mb,me,cfg={}):
    tmp=rs&M32
    v=dict(tmp=tmp,ra=ra,sh=sh,mb=mb,me=me)
    if cfg.get('shpred',lambda v:v['sh'])(v):
        if not 1<=sh<=31: raise Bad('UB shift')
        tmp=((tmp<<sh)|(tmp>>(32-sh)))&M32
    v.update(tmp=tmp)
    if cfg.get('highpred',lambda v:v['mb']>v['me'])(v):
        h=cfg.get('highword',lambda v,rs:v['tmp'])(v,rs)
        low=cfg.get('lowpres',lambda v:v['ra'])(v)
        ra=((low&M32)|(h<<32))&M64
    for _ in range(65):
        if not 0<=mb<32: raise Bad('UB shift')
        mask=1<<(31-mb)
        v.update(ra=ra,mb=mb)
        part=cfg.get('insert',lambda v:v['tmp'])(v)
        ra=((ra&~mask)|(part&mask))&M64
        v.update(ra=ra,mb=mb)
        if cfg.get('breakpred',lambda v:v['mb']==v['me'])(v): return ra
        mb+=1
        v.update(mb=mb)
        if cfg.get('resetpred',lambda v:v['mb']==32)(v): mb=0
    raise Bad('loop')
def dm(rs,ra,sh,mb,cfg={}):
    s=rs
    v=dict(sh=sh,mb=mb,ra=ra,s=s)
    n=cfg.get('ninit',lambda v:v['sh'])(v)
    for _ in range(66):
        v.update(n=n,s=s)
        yes=cfg.get('rotpred',lambda v:v['n']"'!=0)(v)
        n-=1
        if not yes: break
        b=cfg.get('"'bit',lambda v:(v['s']>>63)&1)(v)
        s=((s<<1)|b)&M64
    else: raise Bad('loop')
    v.update(n=n,s=s)
    m=cfg.get('mstart',lambda v:v['mb'])(v)
    tmp=0
    for _ in range(65):
        if not 0<=m<64: raise Bad('UB shift')
        tmp|=1<<(63-m)
        v.update(m=m,tmp=tmp)
        m=cfg.get('mstep',lambda v:(v['m']+1)&63)(v)
        v.update(m=m)
        if not cfg.get('endpred',lambda v:v['m']"'!=((64-v['"'sh'])&63))(v):
            return ((ra&~tmp)|(tmp&s))&M64
    raise Bad('loop')
def inspect(model,tests,cfg):
    fails=[]; invalid=[]
    for name,args,want in tests:
        try:
            got=model(*args,cfg)
            if got"'!=want: fails.append((name,hex(got),hex(want)))
        except Bad as e: invalid.append((name,str(e)))
    return dict(fails=len(fails),invalid=len(invalid),first=(fails+invalid)[:3])

def read_probe(fn):
    tree=ast.parse((ROOT/'regress'/fn).read_text())
    env={}
    defs={'rotl64','rotl32','mask_b_63','mask_0_e','mask_range','mask32','want_rlwimi','want_rlwinm','want_rldimi','want_rldicl','want_rldicr'}
    names={'M64','SENT','RS_ONES','RS_VAL','MUT_RS','SRC','DESTS','census_combos','mb_me_nowrap','mb_me_wrap','seen','uniq_census'}
    chosen=[]
    census=False
    for node in tree.body:
        if isinstance(node,ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in defs: chosen.append(node)
        elif isinstance(node,ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t,ast.Name) and t.id in names for t in node.targets):
            chosen.append(node)
            if any(isinstance(t,ast.Name) and t.id=='census_combos' for t in node.targets): census=True
        elif census and isinstance(node,ast.For):
            if isinstance(node.target,ast.Name) and node.target.id=='base': census=False
            else: chosen.append(node)
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=chosen,type_ignores=[]),str(fn),'exec'),env)
    tests=[]
    wanted='want_rlwimi' if 'rlwimi' in fn else 'want_rldimi'
    for node in tree.body:
        if not (isinstance(node,ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value,ast.Call) and isinstance(node.value.func,ast.Name) and node.value.func.id=='row'): continue
        call=node.value
        for sub in ast.walk(call.args[2]):
            if isinstance(sub,ast.Call) and isinstance(sub.func,ast.Name) and sub.func.id==wanted:
                args=tuple(eval(compile(ast.Expression(a),str(fn),'eval'),env) for a in sub.args)
                tests.append((ast.literal_eval(call.args[0]),args,env[wanted](*args)))
    src,dst=(RS,SENT) if wanted=='want_rlwimi' else (M64,0)
    tests += [('census '+str(cell),(src,dst,*cell),env[wanted](src,dst,*cell)) for cell in env['uniq_census']]
    return env,tests

class Bad(Exception): pass
def rm(rs,ra,sh,mb,me,cfg={}):
    tmp=rs&M32
    v=dict(tmp=tmp,ra=ra,sh=sh,mb=mb,me=me)
    if cfg.get('shpred',lambda v:v['sh'])(v):
        if not 1<=sh<=31: raise Bad('UB shift')
        tmp=((tmp<<sh)|(tmp>>(32-sh)))&M32
    v.update(tmp=tmp)
    if cfg.get('highpred',lambda v:v['mb']>v['me'])(v):
        h=cfg.get('highword',lambda v,rs:v['tmp'])(v,rs)
        low=cfg.get('lowpres',lambda v:v['ra'])(v)
        ra=((low&M32)|(h<<32))&M64
    for _ in range(65):
        if not 0<=mb<32: raise Bad('UB shift')
        mask=1<<(31-mb)
        v.update(ra=ra,mb=mb)
        part=cfg.get('insert',lambda v:v['tmp'])(v)
        ra=((ra&~mask)|(part&mask))&M64
        v.update(ra=ra,mb=mb)
        if cfg.get('breakpred',lambda v:v['mb']==v['me'])(v): return ra
        mb+=1
        v.update(mb=mb)
        if cfg.get('resetpred',lambda v:v['mb']==32)(v): mb=0
    raise Bad('loop')
def dm(rs,ra,sh,mb,cfg={}):
    s=rs
    v=dict(sh=sh,mb=mb,ra=cfg.get('_ra_index',4),s=s)
    n=cfg.get('ninit',lambda v:v['sh'])(v)
    for _ in range(66):
        v.update(n=n,s=s)
        yes=cfg.get('rotpred',lambda v:v['n']"'!=0)(v)
        n-=1
        if not yes: break
        b=cfg.get('"'bit',lambda v:(v['s']>>63)&1)(v)
        s=((s<<1)|b)&M64
    else: raise Bad('loop')
    v.update(n=n,s=s)
    m=cfg.get('mstart',lambda v:v['mb'])(v)
    tmp=0
    for _ in range(65):
        if not 0<=m<64: raise Bad('UB shift')
        tmp|=1<<(63-m)
        v.update(m=m,tmp=tmp)
        m=cfg.get('mstep',lambda v:(v['m']+1)&63)(v)
        v.update(m=m)
        if not cfg.get('endpred',lambda v:v['m']"'!=((64-v['"'sh'])&63))(v):
            return ((ra&~tmp)|(tmp&s))&M64
    raise Bad('loop')
def inspect(model,tests,cfg):
    fails=[]; invalid=[]
    for name,args,want in tests:
        try:
            got=model(*args,cfg)
            if got"'!=want: fails.append((name,hex(got),hex(want)))
        except Bad as e: invalid.append((name,str(e)))
    return dict(fails=len(fails),invalid=len(invalid),first=(fails+invalid)[:3])
